description: VERIFIED DEFECT — the decision record does not match the code, and THE CODE IS RIGHT. The record (ADR-0004 and the docs that echo it) describes a LiteLLM-inside-the-router posture for vendor wire dispatch. The tree says otherwise: `grep -ril litellm provider-router-erl/` returns NOTHING. The canonical router (Erlang/OTP, ADR-0004) reaches ALL SEVEN native-wire vendors — anthropic, gemini, replicate, elevenlabs, runway, luma, minimax — through a **Rust port program**, `translation/crates/wire` built by `provider-router-erl/build-translator.sh` and driven by `apr_translate.erl` as a supervised external OS process (a PORT, not a NIF, precisely so a panic in third-party wire code cannot take down the node and the always-completes ladder stays a structural property rather than a claim about someone else's Rust). LiteLLM appears ONLY in the SUPERSEDED Python router, behind `AGORA_LITELLM=1`, where it makes exactly 2 of 7 vendors dialable (anthropic/gemini text). So the canonical path is not behind the borrowed one — it is AHEAD of it, 8 (vendor,modality) pairs to 2. The code is right for two independent reasons worth writing down: (1) **LiteLLM cannot embed in the BEAM** without either a Python sidecar on the hot path or a NIF, and either choice destroys one of the two differentiators the router exists for — the always-completes ladder (a rung that cannot take down the node) and pre-dial refusal; (2) **supply chain** — LiteLLM 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 were **backdoored on PyPI in March 2026**, which is disqualifying for an unpinned dependency on a request hot path and is the reason the optional Python extra must stay optional, pinned, and off by default. Also record the untried BETTER option for vendor breadth on the canonical side: **`agentjido/req_llm`** — 554 stars, Apache-2.0, v1.0.0, **21 providers / 1,205 models**, native BEAM (no port, no sidecar), with normalized token accounting and USD cost. It is not adopted here; it is recorded as the candidate a future breadth push should evaluate against widening the Rust codec by hand, because 21 providers of maintained coverage against 7 hand-written ones is the kind of asymmetry that decides a build-vs-adopt call. Scope: DOCS + ROADMAP + the record. No behaviour change, no dependency added, and the byte-for-byte Erlang/Python conformance corpus MUST stay green and unregenerated. The out-of-tree ADR-0004 amendment is the operator's own follow-up; this tasklist makes the in-repo record correct and self-consistent so nothing else has to be believed on trust.
warmup: grep -ril litellm provider-router-erl/ || echo 'ZERO LiteLLM in the canonical router — defect confirmed'

userStories.title: State the dispatch record correctly: the canonical router has zero LiteLLM
userStories.description: Every in-repo document that could leave a reader believing the canonical router dispatches through LiteLLM must say what the code actually does. This is a correction of the record, not a change of design.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/litellm-dispatch-adapter.md opens with an explicit scope correction: the adapter is scoped to the SUPERSEDED Python router only; the canonical Erlang router (ADR-0004) contains zero LiteLLM and dials all seven native-wire vendors through the Rust port program `translation/crates/wire` (built by `build-translator.sh`, driven by `apr_translate.erl`).

The coverage asymmetry is stated with its numbers: the Rust codec covers 8 (vendor,modality) pairs across all seven native-wire vendors, where the LiteLLM adapter makes 2 of 7 dialable (anthropic/gemini text) — so the canonical path is ahead of the borrowed one, not behind it.

The port-not-NIF rationale is preserved and cited rather than restated from scratch: an OS process cannot take down the node, so the always-completes ladder stays a structural property; `apr_translate.erl`'s own module doc is the source.

docs/prior-art.md's provider-router section is corrected to match — its 'measured against LiteLLM' paragraph must not leave the impression that the borrowed adapters are the router's dispatch path of record.

userStories.title: Record why the code is right — embedding cost and supply chain
userStories.description: A correction that only says 'the doc was wrong' invites someone to re-litigate it. Record the two independent reasons the current design is the correct one.
acceptanceCriteria: The record states the embedding argument concretely: LiteLLM cannot live inside the BEAM without a Python sidecar on the hot path or a NIF, and either choice costs one of the two differentiators the router exists for — the always-completes ladder (no rung may take down the node) and per-request pre-dial refusal.

The record states the supply-chain argument: LiteLLM 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 were backdoored on PyPI in March 2026 — disqualifying for an unpinned dependency on a request hot path, and the standing reason the optional Python extra stays optional, version-pinned, and off by default.

The consequence is made concrete rather than left as a moral: the `[litellm]` extra's version constraint is checked and pinned to exclude the compromised releases, or the reason it cannot be is recorded.

Nothing in this story changes runtime behaviour, adds or removes a dependency, or regenerates the byte-for-byte conformance corpus; `make check-router-erl` and `make check-provider-router` both stay green.

userStories.title: Record req_llm as the untried option, and re-order Phase B around the real canonical path
userStories.description: Vendor breadth is a live roadmap phase built on the wrong assumption about which path is canonical. Fix the ordering and name the adopt candidate nobody has evaluated.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/prior-art.md records `agentjido/req_llm` as the untried option for canonical-side vendor breadth, with its facts and their observation date: 554 stars, Apache-2.0, v1.0.0, 21 providers / 1,205 models, native BEAM (no port, no Python sidecar), normalized token accounting and USD cost.

It is recorded as a CANDIDATE, not an adoption: the note states what would have to be evaluated before adopting (whether it can sit below the injected transport boundary without touching the always-completes ladder, pre-dial refusal, the `unpriced` rule, or the KCB manifest) and that 21 maintained providers against 7 hand-written codecs is the asymmetry that would decide it.

ROADMAP.md's Phase B is re-ordered and re-scoped so the canonical Rust `wire` codec (`chief/52`) is the vendor-breadth path of record and the LiteLLM adapter row (`chief/51`) is explicitly scoped to the superseded Python router — with a stated note that `51` is chasing parity the canonical path already has, so it exists only to keep the byte-for-byte corpus meaningful, if at all.
Phase B's prose no longer describes widening 'the one thing the router punts on' as a LiteLLM story, and a `chief/70`-style row for evaluating req_llm is added to Phase B or the Ongoing block.
